title: Invoice smoothing for sub-hour pool churn and overrun protection
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem statement: We frequently observe unexpected invoice spikes for customers on Dedicated pools when capacity is scaled or migrated within billing windows shorter than an hour (sub-hour churn). Root causes: (1) immediate charging for observed physical capacity usage combined with coarse-hour rounding for reserved throughput; (2) overrun events that trigger burst debits followed by SLA credits posted in separate reconciliation runs, producing confusing doubled line-items; (3) current per-minute aggregation and ledger compacting causes transient duplicates when a tenant is moved between pool shards during the same minute. Business impact: customers receive noisy invoices, leading to support tickets and finance disputes, and platform teams face churn on retro credits and manual reconciliations.

Goals: create a predictable, auditable invoicing behavior for dedicated capacity under sub-hour churn without changing cost economics (no revenue leakage). Provide clear ledger primitives that make immediate charges explainable and ensure SLA credits are applied in a way that avoids double-billing artifacts on the same invoice cycle.

Proposed design summary: "invoice smoothing corridor"
- Maintain a time-weighted reserved-capacity allocation per tenant (microsecond-accurate endpoints) rather than coarse hour rounding. Use an event-sourced microledger for each tenant that records ReservationStart/ReservationEnd, OverrunDebit, and SLAAdjustment events. The ledger is append-only and idempotent keyed by (tenant, reservation_id, event_seq).
- Implement a short-duration "invoice smoothing corridor" (configurable, default 10 minutes) that caps immediate invoiceable overrun exposure: when an overrun occurs the platform records the debit but defers hard invoicing until the corridor expires. Within the corridor we capture additional events (migrations, scale-downs, SLA-eligible degradations) and amortize costs across the corridor window so transient churn costs are spread and any subsequent SLA credits are netted before the invoice line is finalized.
- When corridor ends, run per-tenant amortization that: (a) computes time-proportional reserved cost share; (b) nets any SLA adjustment events generated during the corridor; (c) emits final InvoiceLine items and marks ledger events as settled. If the tenant churns across pool shards during the corridor, the event-sourced ledger deduplicates based on reservation_id.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict realtime billing (current approach) yields immediate revenue visibility but produces noisy invoices on churn — rejected by finance & support.
- Longer corridor windows (>1 hour) smooth more but delay accurate charge visibility for customers — unacceptable for high-usage tenants. 10 minutes chosen as compromise; parameterizable per tier.

Implementation details:
- New microledger service (billing-ledger) with API: append_event(tenant, reservation_id, event_type, amount, meta, idempotency_key).
- Light-weight in-memory corridor cache per tenant in gateway to collect events for N minutes; durable mirror persisted to ledger and Kafka.
- Reconciliation job (billing-finalizer) runs per-corridor expiry and produces invoice lines, posts to billing database and emits webhooks for Console and Invoicing UI.
- Metrics: invoice_variance_rolling_7d, corridor_hit_rate, deferred_exposure_total, reconciliation_latency_ms.
- Tests: unit tests for idempotency, chaos tests for pool migration mid-corridor, e2e integration with billing UI showing before/after line items.

Migration path and customer opt-in:
- Phase 1 (canary): apply corridor to 5 low-risk Dedicated tenants (non-enterprise) for 3 weeks; finance to verify invoice parity over month boundary.
- Phase 2: roll to Reserved customers with 1-day notice and enable configurable corridor length in Console.

Observability and troubleshooting:
- Add Console view "Smoothing corridors" showing active corridors, accumulated debits, and pending adjustments.
- Add audit log entries linking ledger events to GitHub PRs and incident IDs for manual reconciliations.

Open questions:
1) How to present deferred vs final line-items in Console and downstream invoice export? (design input requested from Finance/PM)
2) Should corridor window be dynamically adaptive based on churn signal? (future work)

Acceptance criteria:
- No net revenue change in billing-aggregates for canary customers over 30 days (finance verified).
- Reduction in invoice-related support tickets for canary cohort by >=60%.
- Reconciliation latency for corridor finalization < 2 minutes after expiry.
updates: 2026-02-22: Observed invoice spike for tenant T-1043 after three rapid pool resizes; reproduced locally using pool-sim harness.
2026-02-25: Design review with PM (Janelle Park) and Finance (Marco Ruiz). Finance agrees smoothing corridor acceptable if no revenue leakage; requested auditability for each adjustment.
2026-02-27: Spike root-cause narrowed to duplicate per-minute compaction + immediate overrun debiting during shard migration. Created prototype ledger events to dedupe via reservation_id.
2026-03-05: Prototype commit pushed (github.com/redwood-inference/billing-ledger PR #5678) demonstrating idempotent append and corridor cache. Benchmark shows <5ms median append latency.
2026-03-08: PM requested Console mockups for deferred line-items — linked in attachments. Finance suggested including 'expected final charge' annotations.
2026-03-10: Bench tests with 10k churn events/day show invoice variance reduced 12% and corridor memory footprint acceptable (~80MB for 10k active corridors).
2026-03-12: Moved ticket to In Progress. Implementation split into two PRs: ledger and finalizer. Assigned to Liam for ownership of production rollout plan.
notes: Deliver a smoothing corridor that reduces noisy invoices while preserving exact accounting; prioritized as P1 due to customer complaints and finance alignment.
